PART I

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Our business is subject to a number of risks, including intense competition in the markets in which we operate. If we are unable to compete effectively, our revenue and market share could decline materially. We also face risks related to supply chain disruptions, which have increased in frequency over the past two fiscal years. Additionally, our international operations expose us to foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations and evolving regulatory requirements in the jurisdictions where we operate, including new data privacy legislation that could increase our compliance costs significantly. We rely on a limited number of suppliers for certain key components, and the loss of any of these suppliers could disrupt our ability to manufacture our products on schedule.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Revenue increased 12% year over year, driven primarily by strong demand in our core product lines. Gross margin improved by 150 basis points due to favorable input cost trends and manufacturing efficiencies. Operating expenses grew slower than revenue, reflecting continued discipline in discretionary spending. We believe our liquidity position remains strong, with sufficient cash on hand to fund operations for the foreseeable future.

Item 9A. Controls and Procedures

Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures. Based on that evaluation, our CEO and CFO concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of the end of the period covered by this report.
